title: Censor Bleep
blurb: The 1000 Hz censor bleep, television's universal way of saying you know exactly what word that was. Broadcasters standardised on a single clean sine tone because nothing else is so impossible to mistake for anything else, and the internet inherited it as comedy punctuation. This is the full one-second version, ready for bleeping out names, brands, or a friend's genuinely indefensible opinion. It is the sound Bleepboard is named after. It also has a strange property: applied to almost anything, the censored version lands harder than whatever was actually said.
origin: Broadcast TV censorship tone, standardized around a 1 kHz sine wave.
